b1plus-causative.title: Causative: -tir / -dir / -t
b1plus-causative.explanation: The causative marks "making/letting someone do something": o'qimoq (to read/study) → o'qitmoq (to teach, literally "to make [someone] study"), yozmoq (to write) → yozdirmoq (to have [someone] write), kiymoq (to wear) → kiydirmoq (to dress someone).
b1plus-causative.fact: O'qitmoq ("to teach") is itself a causative built on o'qimoq ("to read/study") -- Uzbek doesn't have a separate root for "teach" at all, it's grammatically just "to cause to study".

dialogue.en: Who had you write this article?
My manager had me write it.

b1plus-until.title: Until: -guncha
b1plus-until.explanation: -guncha (with voiced variants -kuncha/-quncha) means "until [X happens]": u kelguncha kutaman (I'll wait until he/she comes), ish tugaguncha ishladik (we worked until the job was finished).
b1plus-until.fact: The same suffix also covers "the sooner ~, the better" comparisons in fixed phrases like ko'p gapirguncha, kam gapir ("rather than talking a lot, talk little") -- "until" and "rather than" turn out to share one grammatical shape in Uzbek.

b1plus-before-after.title: Before/After a Verb: -madan oldin / -gandan keyin
b1plus-before-after.explanation: To sequence two actions, Uzbek attaches oldin ("before") to a negative-form-looking but neutral -madan and keyin ("after") to the -gan participle: ovqatlanmasdan oldin qo'l yuvaman (I wash my hands before eating), ovqatlanganimdan keyin dam olaman (after eating I rest).
b1plus-before-after.fact: -madan oldin looks like it contains the negative -ma-, but it isn't a negation here at all -- it's a fixed fossilized pattern meaning "before doing", one of several places where a suffix's shape and its usual meaning have quietly drifted apart.

dialogue.en: What do you do before sleeping?
I sleep after reading a book.

b1plus-optative.title: Wish: -sa edi
b1plus-optative.explanation: Adding edi (the past form of "to be") after the conditional -sa turns a condition into a wish about something not currently true: vaqtim bo'lsa edi... (if only I had time...), u shu yerda bo'lsa edi (if only he/she were here).
b1plus-optative.fact: This is the same -sa used for ordinary "if" clauses -- edi is the only thing that shifts the meaning from a real possibility to a wistful wish about something that isn't the case, much like English swaps "have" for "had" to mark the same shift.

dialogue.en: If only I had more time.

b1plus-permission.title: Permission/Possibility: -sa bo'ladi
b1plus-permission.explanation: -sa bo'ladi (literally "if ~, it becomes/works") asks or grants permission: bu yerda o'tirsa bo'ladimi? (may I sit here?), kirsa bo'ladi (you may enter). The negative bo'lmaydi denies it: bu yerda chekilsa bo'lmaydi (smoking is not allowed here).
b1plus-permission.fact: Because bo'lmoq means "to become/turn out", this construction literally asks "if [I do this], will it turn out okay?" -- permission in Uzbek is phrased as a check on the outcome, not a direct request for someone's approval the way English "may I" is.

dialogue.en: May I take a photo here?

The mother dressed her child.
The manager had the employee prepare a report.
He/she taught me how to drive.
My mother taught me how to cook.
They made us complete this task.
He/she made the children sing a song.
I had the mechanic repair the car.
The director had the employees write a report.
He/she had me read through the book.
The mother dressed her daughter.
We'll wait until he/she comes.
We worked until the job was finished.
I prepared until the exam started.
We were on the road until it got light.
I won't calm down until this issue is resolved.

items.uz: U uyga yetib boguncha yomg'ir yog'di.
items.en: It rained until he/she got home.
We set the table until the food was ready.
The mother waited until the child fell asleep.
I won't rest until I finish this task.
I sat and waited until my turn came.
It will be hot until autumn comes.
I didn't talk until he/she apologized.
I wash my hands before eating.
I read a book before sleeping.
I have breakfast before going to work.
I prepared well before the exam.
I rest after eating.
I go home after finishing work.
We'll talk after you arrive.
I was happy after taking the exam.
I'll let you know after I see him/her.
I got to work after returning from the trip.

items.uz: Kitobni o'qishdan oldin uning haqida so'radim.
items.en: I asked about the book before reading it.
I drink tea after waking up.
If only I had more time.
If only he/she were here.
If only I had enough money.

items.uz: Bu imkoniyatni qo'ldan boy bermasam edi.
items.en: If only I hadn't missed this opportunity.
If only the weather were good.

items.uz: Men bu haqida oldinroq bilsam edi.
items.en: If only I had known about this earlier.
If only he/she understood me.
If only I could come next year.
If only this illness were curable.
If only I could return to my youth.
If only I had done this differently.
If only I could talk with you more.
May I sit here?
May I open the window?
May I take this book?
You may take a photo here.
Smoking is not allowed here.
Is it okay not to come tomorrow?
May I ask this question?
May I go home early?
You can't park a car here.
You may call me.
It's also fine if you don't come today.

items.uz: Bu masalani keyinroq hal qilsak bo'ladi.
items.en: We can resolve this issue later.
